calls.body: The Lightning have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Kraken near the bottom. Expect the Lightning to spend more of the night in the Kraken’s end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

SEA.head: We gave Seattle only a 30% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Hedman wins it in overtime
paras: Ryan Winterton got the scoring started for the Kraken early in the first, but Brandon Hagel tied it up for Tampa Bay late in the period. The Kraken’s Brandon Montour left early in the second period and didn’t return. The next day, he was listed as day to day with a lower-body injury. Hagel scored his second of the night early in the period to put the Lightning ahead 2-1. Jared McCann tied it up for Seattle on the power play early in the third. Ilya Mikheyev scored his 100th NHL goal midway through the period to put the Bolts back ahead 3-2. Matty Beniers tied it 3-3 for Seattle with a little over four minutes left. Victor Hedman won it just over two minutes into overtime.

The Lightning had the better of the chances, outshooting the Kraken 35-27. Andrei Vasilevskiy made 24 saves for the Lightning, and Philipp Grubauer stopped 31 of 35 at the other end. The Lightning moved to 5-2-0, third in the Atlantic, while the Kraken fell to 5-2-1, third in the Pacific.

items.text: The Kraken’s three-game winning streak is over.
Brandon Hagel has a point in all seven of his games against Seattle since 2023-24.
Victor Hedman scored his first goal of the season, his first since Feb 28 (15 games played since).
